thread:
sophia: Quick FYI — nightly kernel sift found a cluster of candidates that regress 12-22% on KV longseq paths on Ampere64. Job: ci-kern-sift/214567.
raj: saw that. attaching perf-bot summary: "kv_longseq: p50 +18% p95 +24%" :grimacing: 
perf-bot: CI summary for ci-kern-sift/214567 — failures: 6/120 microbench cases; flaky: 2; seed: 20260316
oliver: Hmm, are these the new post-simd remap kernels? Might be worse cache line behavior for big k-v caches.
anya: I repro locally on a8g (ampere) with seqlen=4096; flamegraph looks like KV lookup + memcpy hotpath.
oliver: can you paste the flamegraph link?
anya: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/214567 — top shows memcpy at 42%, kv_lookup at 28%, kernel_dispatch overhead 11%
marcos: CI harness note — the microbench uses batch_size=1, kvsize=8MB, seqlen distro sampled skewed to long tail. We should try batch=4 to match runtime batching.
sophia: Good point — the runtime's seqlen-based path switches at 1024/2048, so a lot of these samples are hitting the 'longseq' codepaths in the runtime. Could be kernel selection mismatch.
raj: Proposed short checklist:
- run harness with batch=4
- enable kernel-fallback logging in CI
- run candidate kernels with -O2 vs -Ofast to check vectorization issues
- add simple memcpy regression threshold at p50
oliver: I'll open a quick PR to adjust harness config and add a per-arch gating rule. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/810
sophia: For gating: suggest "reject if p95 regress > 15% OR any p50 >10% AND reproduced on ampere64". Thoughts?
marcos: Agree but let's make an exception window: skip gating for avx512-only candidates unless we have avx512 infra. Also add a "kv-warmup" phase to microbench: run 3 warm iterations to populate KV cache.
anya: Here's a small repro command I've used:
```
./bench_kv --kernel=KANDYV2 --seqlen=4096 --kv=8M --batch=1 --iters=2000 --warm=3
```
add --batch=4 to compare.
perf-bot: Note: recorded job id 214567. Artifact: s3://redwood-ci/ci-kern-sift/214567/artifacts.tar.gz
raj: I'll kick an orthogonal run with batch=4 + warmup and attach flamegraphs. If regressions persist, we should fail the candidate and roll back autotune picks for the kernel family.
sophia: Thanks — let's reconvene after the run. If it fails, we need a short postmortem and a temporary routing rule to send longseq traffic to fallback kernels in production. :thumbsup:
